# Welcome {.unnumbered}

This guide is for the co-chairs of the annual AP-LS conference. It explains
how the conference pages on [ap-ls.org](https://ap-ls.org) are put together
and how to keep them current through your conference year.

You do not need to know R or Quarto for routine updates. The conference
pages are plain text files with some structure around them. If you can edit
a document and rename a file, you can handle most of the work in this guide.

## What this guide covers

- How the conference pages fit together and where each file lives
- What to update at each point in the conference year
- How to open the call for proposals and add preconference workshops
- How to hand the site over to the next year's co-chairs

It covers the mechanics only. Decisions about content, such as deadlines,
rates, and the theme of the call for proposals, stay with you and the
conference committee.

## The two reference documents

Two files in the website folder carry the full detail. This guide points to
them instead of repeating them:

- `UPDATING.md` in the project root covers setup, previewing, images, and
  how changes reach the live site.
- `conferences/_template/README.md` is the checklist for starting a new
  conference year.

When this guide and those files ever disagree, trust the files. They are
updated every time the site changes.
